rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance: annual CPI-based rent increase cap
rules.requirement: At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not request or receive an increase above the CPI-U percentage change (NY-northern NJ-Long Island, from 15 months to 3 months before the month of the increase), and never above 4%. No more than one increase in any consecutive 12-month period regardless of tenant turnover, ownership change or vacancy. The annual increase is barred if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance or the landlord has not registered. The landlord must give the tenant and the Rent Regulation Officer written notice at least 30 days ahead. Surcharges (tax, major new improvement, utilities) and hardship increases are separate processes, and Board-granted increases within 12 months may not exceed 25% in total. Excess rent must be rebated, and violations are fined.
rules.key_value: Annual increase capped at the CPI-U change (15 months prior to 3 months prior), maximum 4%; 30 days' written notice to tenant and Rent Regulation Officer; one increase per 12 months; 25% overall limit on Board-granted increases in a year

new_construction_exemption.basis: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from limits on periodic increases for the shorter of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion of construction (Certificate of Occupancy); 30 years if no initial mortgage financing

unverifiable_exemptions: Units under a landlord contract with a governmental agency that regulates rent
Units rehabilitated under federal/state Rental Rehabilitation Programs receiving Section 8 or vouchers
Vacant dwellings exempted for 5 years after substantial rehabilitation (Board determination)
Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt by Rent Control Board certification
coverage.summary: All multiple dwellings are subject to rent control. Exempt: public housing, hotel/motel space rented day-to-day, commercial space, newly constructed multiple dwellings (up to 30 years), rehabilitated vacant dwellings (5 years), certain Section 8 rehabilitation units, and units under governmental agency rent-regulation contracts.
coverage.owner_conditions: The definition of owner-occupied (four units or less with the owner residing in one) appears, but the text does not list owner-occupied dwellings among the exemptions.
coverage.other_conditions: Landlord must register annually and the dwelling must be in substantial compliance to take the annual increase.

rules.exemptions: Public housing; hotel/motel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings (shorter of initial mortgage amortization or 30 years from completion of construction, by filing with the Rent Control Board); vacant dwellings substantially rehabilitated (5 years); certain Section 8 rehabilitation units; units under a governmental agency rent-regulation contract.
rules.effective_date_note: The chapter was first adopted September 4, 1985 and continues in force from October 19, 1988. The current CPI/4% provision was amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I; the text does not say when the 4% cap itself began.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.review_note: Section 19:2-7.1 cross-references registration at subsection 19:1-10, which appears to be an erroneous cite for 19:2-9.8.
rules.source_notes: Official code text; the chapter heading is dated October 3, 2026.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance: retaliatory eviction bar
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under the rent control chapter. The statement of policy also ties rent control to the fear of eviction without just cause, but the chapter lists no allowed causes, notice contents or relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: No eviction action as reprisal for tenant's efforts to secure or enforce rights under the rent control chapter

coverage.summary: Applies to dwelling units subject to the Newark rent control chapter (all multiple dwellings, less exempt dwellings).

rules.effective_date_note: Section last amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I; original effective date not stated for this section.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
rules.review_note: Reprisal protection only; no general just-cause list in this chapter.

rules.title: Newark protected tenancy for seniors and disabled tenants facing condo/co-op conversion eviction
rules.requirement: The Rent Control Office Administrator accepts applications from senior citizen or disabled tenants to determine eligibility for protected tenancy status against eviction resulting from condominium or cooperative conversion. Eligibility follows the state Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22). The landlord pays a $350 hearing officer fee and a $30 notification fee per tenant.
rules.key_value: Protected tenancy status from eviction due to condo/co-op conversion for eligible seniors and disabled tenants

unverifiable_exemptions: Tenant eligibility as a senior or disabled tenant under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22
coverage.summary: Senior citizen and disabled tenants in buildings undergoing condominium or cooperative conversion.
coverage.other_conditions: Eligibility determined by state protected tenancy standards.

rules.effective_date_note: Section last amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I; original effective date not stated.
rules.quoted_span: The Administrator of the Office of Rent Control shall be empowered to accept applications from senior citizen tenants or disabled tenants for the purpose of determining their eligibility for protected tenancy status from eviction resulting from condominium or cooperative conversions.
rules.review_note: Administrative process implementing state law; the substantive protection comes from N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22 et seq.

result.doc_summary: Official text of Newark Rev. Gen. Ord. ch. 19:2 (Rent Control Regulations; Rent Control Board), as amended through Ord. 6PSF-I (2024) and 6PSF-B (5-20-2026). It caps annual rent increases at the CPI-U change with a 4% maximum, and sets out surcharges, hardship increases, rent decreases, registration, inspection and habitability certificates, new-construction and rehabilitation exemptions, and penalties. Eviction-related content is limited to a retaliatory eviction bar and condo-conversion protected tenancy administration. The document has no provisions on security deposits, application fees, screening restrictions or algorithmic rent setting.
